item.title: The Top 5 Longreads of the Week
item.description: In this edition: Bezos, paper, scissors; feast or famine; one reason to stay here; any way you slice it; the real Winter Olympics, and more.

item.title: Why the Future of Movies Lives on Letterboxd
item.description: "If Rotten Tomatoes has become a tool of Hollywood’s homogenizing marketing machinery, Letterboxd is something else: a cinephilic hive buzzing with authentic enthusiasm and heterogeneous tastes."

item.title: Venom in His Veins
item.description: "Bill Haast, the Florida man who tried to milk medical miracles from deadly snakes."

item.title: Deepfaking Orson Welles’s Mangled Masterpiece
item.description: "Will an A.I. restoration of 'The Magnificent Ambersons' right a historic wrong or desecrate a classic?"

item.title: He Called Himself an ‘Untouchable Hacker God’. But Who Was Behind the Biggest Crime Finland Has Ever Known?
item.description: "How would you feel if your therapist’s notes – your darkest thoughts and deepest feelings – were exposed to the world? For 33,000 Finnish people, that became a terrifying reality, with deadly consequences."

item.title: The Return of the Night Sky
item.description: "Artificial light is spreading faster than scientists once thought, reshaping ecosystems and human health. Now activists, designers, and city officials around the world are beginning to push back."

item.title: Seeing is Believing: A Reading List on Making Meaning from Data
item.description: Eight stories on the power and beauty of visual communication.

item.title: The Babies Kept in a Mysterious Los Angeles Mansion
item.description: "A wealthy couple obtained dozens of children through surrogates. Did they want a family, or something else?"

item.title: Everyone Is Stealing TV
item.description: "Fed up with increasing subscription prices, viewers embrace rogue streaming boxes."

item.title: America Isn’t Ready for What AI Will Do to Jobs
item.description: "Does anyone have a plan for what happens next?"
